description: Key facts a correct lesson on each Power Systems topic must state. Every fact was taken from the fetched text of the source page named with it (the quote is checked by `npm run golden:check`). Patterns are case-insensitive regular expressions matched against the lesson text after LaTeX backslashes and braces are removed.
subject: power-systems

facts.claim: Voltage is stepped up for transmission to cut losses

source.quote: the voltage is often increased for transmission, then reduced for local distribution

facts.claim: AC current crowds near the conductor surface

source.quote: the current density is largest near the surface of the conductor

facts.claim: Higher frequency → smaller skin depth

source.quote: as frequency increases, current flow becomes more concentrated near the surface, resulting in less skin depth

facts.claim: Ferranti effect: receiving-end voltage rises above sending end on a long lightly loaded line

source.quote: the Ferranti effect is the increase in voltage occurring at the receiving end of a very long

facts.claim: It is due to line capacitance (charging current)

source.quote: both line inductance and capacitance are responsible for this phenomenon

facts.claim: A line is modelled as a two-port network

source.quote: a two-port network (a kind of four-terminal network or quadripole)

facts.claim: A conductor hanging between supports forms a catenary (approximated by a parabola)

source.quote: Flexible conductors supported at their ends approximate the form of a catenary

facts.claim: Conductors are carried by towers or poles

source.quote: suspended by towers or poles

facts.claim: An insulator does not let current flow freely

source.quote: An electrical insulator is a material in which electric current does not flow freely

facts.claim: A power cable has insulated conductors in a sheath

source.quote: usually held together in a single bundle with an insulating sheath

facts.claim: Per-unit = actual value / base value

source.quote: the expression of system quantities as fractions of a defined base unit quantity

facts.claim: Per-unit values are the same on both sides of a transformer

source.quote: quantities expressed as per-unit do not change when they are referred from one side of a transformer to the other

facts.claim: Load flow finds bus voltage magnitudes and angles, and line flows

source.quote: the magnitude and phase angle of the voltage at each bus

facts.claim: The equations are non-linear, so iterative methods are used

source.quote: The problem is non-linear because the power flow into load impedances is a function of the square of the applied voltages

facts.claim: A symmetrical fault affects all three phases equally

source.quote: a fault may affect all phases equally, which is a "symmetric fault"

facts.claim: Faults on some phases are asymmetrical and harder to analyse

source.quote: If only some phases are affected, the resulting "asymmetric fault" becomes more complicated to analyse

facts.claim: The power (rotor, torque) angle

source.quote: The angle between the two is known as the power angle, torque angle, or rotor angle

facts.claim: Rotor inertia governs the swing

source.quote: is the total moment of inertia of the rotor mass

facts.claim: Economic dispatch minimises generation cost

source.quote: Dispatching power generation in this way, known as economic dispatch, minimizes the cost of production of electricity

facts.claim: Units with the lowest marginal (incremental) cost are loaded first

source.quote: those with the lowest marginal costs are the first sources to be brought online

facts.claim: HVDC suits long distances: fewer conductors, lower losses

source.quote: HVDC lines are commonly used for long-distance power transmission, since they require fewer conductors and incur less power loss

facts.claim: Halving current at double voltage cuts losses fourfold

source.quote: using half the current at double the voltage reduces the line losses by a factor of 4
